name: targeted-1026-203339
hypothesis: Failure pattern: the player cannot read what story options cost the three promotion inputs, so careers stay at the entry level and are dismissed for capability at month 24. Evidence from the champion's 6 latest race digests: both early exits (ladd-00001, scre-00004; its only exits in its latest 12 games) are month-24 capability dismissals of players not promoted in the first year, while the 4 games promoted at the first or second review all completed (lab tally: 12/14 completed after a first-review promotion, 0/13 when not promoted by the second). There were 14 entry-level reviews in the digests. All 5 promotions had Output at the highest value the game shows at that level, with Skill and Network at or next to theirs. Each of the 9 misses had Output or Network below that high (Output in 6), and 2 also had Skill short. In all 9 misses the short input had been at its high after the last Energy phase, or reached it in a later story, and a later story choice took it away; on every losing choice the player's note expected no cost or a gain. Losing choices by miss: rest while work waited, at Health 5 to 9, with the work called non-urgent (4 misses); a note or record written for others, read as free goodwill or visible results (3); a side review or meeting, read as a relationship or visibility chance (2); learning on the job (1); passing up learning (2); turning down, correcting or going over a colleague, including a light touch with an intern meant to protect Output (4). In at least 4 of the 5 promotions, the same kind of loss happened before the review and a later helping or delivering story happened to win it back, so promotion was luck. The player also misreads a full input as weak. In all 6 games its notes call Network the weakest while it sat at its entry-level high, and 4 of 6 spent first-quarter Energy or the main action lifting it. Meanwhile 5 of the 6 first-review windows began with Skill or Output still short after that phase. Why the change fixes it: the champion's story rule, 'avoid downsides on protected dimensions; prefer helping the weakest', cannot protect inputs whose downsides the player cannot see, and it points the player at an input that is already full. The change gives the player cost cues that fit every losing and every restoring choice in these digests. Time away from your own deliverables lowers Output, and finishing or showing them raises it. Turning down, correcting or going over a colleague lowers Network, and helping, including or thanking one raises it. Passing up learning lowers Skill. With these cues, full inputs count as protected and only short ones as weak, so the player can fill the short inputs, keep the full ones through the run-up to a review, and deliberately win back a point that an honest choice cost. In scre-00004 the only loss before its second review was rest at Health 7, with an option to stay and finish declined; avoiding it gives a promotion by the second review, after which 4 of 4 digested careers completed. In scre-00002, 2 of the 3 losing choices before its first review had alternatives without that cost. Limit: in ladd-00001 the decisive choices had a cost on every option, so no story rule saves that career. Differences from earlier ideas: targeted-1026-201334 bans two named trades (rest at comfortable Health, learning with Skill stalled) until the first promotion, but 8 of the 9 misses include a losing choice outside those trades, and the player did not see them as trades. f7-delivery-stories-v1 (2/4, Q 46.5) ranked delivery options only after an input had fallen. This variant corrects the player's prediction of costs before any loss, at every level, and keeps the champion's other text verbatim.
change: Adds a short Story costs section saying that promotion reads Skill, Network and Output at each review, that each stops at a ceiling for the level (full), and how story wording predicts their cost or gain: time away from own deliverables lowers Output, turning down, correcting or going over a colleague lowers Network, passing up learning lowers Skill; finishing or showing own work and helping colleagues raise them. Balance then lifts only inputs that are not full, and its story rule counts Skill, Network and Output as protected, takes the honest option even when it costs one and wins the point back at the next chance; everything else is the champion's text verbatim (605 words, champion 393).
predicted_behaviour: Story notes name what an option costs Skill, Network or Output, or cite Story costs. With the inputs full, the player declines rest while work waits at mid-range Health, side reviews, notes for others and learning on the job, and picks the option that keeps its own deliverables moving. After an honest refusal or correction it takes the next helping, including or thanking option to win back the point. At the entry level, Energy and main actions stop going to a Network that sits at its ceiling; they go to a short input, or to Health recovery and Defuse. More entry-level reviews find all three inputs at their high. Promotions by the second review rise above the champion's 4 of 6 digested games, and month-24 dismissals fall below its 2 in 12. Disclosure choices, Defuse after risk signals and Health recovery stay as in the champion, so risk control and resilience in completed games hold near 74 and 100.
refutation: Refuted if, over 8 or more race games, month-24 dismissals do not fall below the champion's 2 in 12 and promotions by the second review do not rise, or if the mean score is below the champion's by more than the decision margin. Also refuted if blackouts or trust-crisis exits appear (champion 0 in 12), or if risk control in completed games falls clearly below 74; either would mean the cost reading pushed the player off healthy or honest choices. The mechanism is refuted if notes name the costs and the inputs stay at their high, yet entry-level reviews still miss promotion. Uninformative if notes never name story costs and losses of full inputs before reviews stay as frequent as in the champion's digests (at least one in every miss); then the rule was not executed.
